job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Ravi lives in a village where he works as a seasonal farm labourer, planting seeds during the monsoon and harvesting crops in winter. Between these busy seasons, he often struggles to find work because farming does not provide daily tasks throughout the entire year. Seeking better opportunities, his cousin Meena moved to the city. Meena works as a street vendor selling vegetables. She works long hours every day, often standing in the heat, but she earns very little profit after paying for her supplies. She is not lazy; she works harder than most, yet her income remains unstable. In the same city, Meena’s friend Sunita works in a large office. Sunita has a permanent job with a contract that includes medical leave and a pension. However, not everyone in the city has such security. Many people like Meena work in the informal sector without any written contracts, paid leave, or retirement benefits. The city offers diverse ways to earn a living, but the quality of these jobs varies greatly, ranging from secure office roles to the daily struggle of street vending.

items.evidence: Between these busy seasons, he often struggles to find work because farming does not provide daily tasks throughout the entire year.
items.q: Why does Ravi often struggle to find work between the planting and harvest seasons?
options: Farm work comes only in certain seasons
He is unwilling to take other jobs
Farm work is spread evenly over the months
His employer pays him a fixed salary
items.explain: Farming does not give daily tasks all year, so labourers like Ravi find little work between seasons.

wrong.why: thinks landless labourers do not want to work
thinks farm work is the same every month
thinks village workers always get a salary from an employer

items.evidence: She is not lazy; she works harder than most, yet her income remains unstable.
items.q: Meena earns very little. Which reason does the passage give for her low income?
options: Her profit is small after buying supplies
She does not work long hours
She sells her vegetables for free
She has a fixed monthly salary
items.explain: Meena works hard, but after paying for her supplies she keeps very little profit.

wrong.why: thinks street vendors are poor because they are lazy
thinks vendors sell for free and buy nothing
thinks city casual workers get a fixed salary

items.evidence: Sunita has a permanent job with a contract that includes medical leave and a pension.
items.q: How is Sunita's job different from Meena's work as a street vendor?
options: Sunita has a contract with benefits
Sunita works longer hours each day
Meena has paid leave and a pension
Meena works in a large office
items.explain: Sunita's contract gives medical leave and a pension, while Meena's informal work has no such benefits.

wrong.why: assumes office work means longer hours
thinks all city jobs give leave and pensions
mixes up who has the office job

items.evidence: Many people like Meena work in the informal sector without any written contracts, paid leave, or retirement benefits.
items.q: Meena falls ill and cannot sell for a week. What will most likely happen?
options: She loses her daily earnings that week
She receives a pension from her employer
She is paid a fixed salary anyway
items.explain: Informal workers like Meena have no paid leave, so days without work mean no income.

wrong.why: thinks all city jobs give medical leave
thinks pensions come from any job
thinks casual workers get fixed monthly pay
